params.body:
From Nightwatch (issue 19, this afternoon): Amazonbot asked for `/website/detail/ODM2OQ==` and got a 500.

That address is missing the `&` the detail route expects, so it falls through to `website/{dealer_hash}/{params?}` with the word "detail" as the hash. `Crypt::decryptString` throws on anything that is not a valid encrypted value, nobody caught it, and the visitor got a 500 while the log got an error that is not an error. The same held for a valid hash of a dealer who no longer exists: `find` returned `null` and the next line read a field off it.

These pages are public and followed by search engines, so an old, truncated or invented address is an ordinary event, not an incident. A 500 says the fault is ours; a wrong link is the visitor's.

One place now turns a hash into a dealer — `dealerIdFromHash` catches `DecryptException` as a 404, `websiteDealer` answers 404 when the dealer is gone — and every public entry point of the website module goes through it: the catalogue, the detail page, the search, the model and body-style lists behind the search bar, and the lead form. The two encryption shapes stay side by side because the blades make both: `Crypt::encryptString` for the detail page and the mode button, `Crypt::encrypt` for the search form and the dropdown lists. The colon case (a hash that carries more than the id) moved into the helper unchanged.

New rule R S2-5.24, and `AWrongWebsiteLinkIsNotACrashTest` pins it with Amazonbot's own address as the first case, plus a hash that is not an encrypted value, a truncated one, a valid hash of a deleted dealer, the detail page, the model list, and a real hash that still opens the site. Checked against the unfixed code: six of the seven failed.

Fixes bevinding een-oud-website-adres-geeft-500.

params.title: A wrong website link is a 404, not a crash
